title: clean vault pair — source file + byte-identical vault copy + matching ledger row
spec_case: V1: a fake vault dir with note.md, a source file with identical bytes, and a ledger row matching source path + source sha256 + vault path + vault sha256. Expected: VERIFIED.
intent: A fake vault dir holds note.md; a source file holds identical bytes; the ledger tests/vault/ledger-V1.tsv holds one row whose source path + source sha256 + vault path + vault sha256 all match. Expected verdict: VERIFIED (receipt moved-to-obsidian). Under the r2 vocabulary the installed tools/souji-verify.sh reports SAFE + moved-to-obsidian for the same inputs — see crosscheck.
path_convention: substitute @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the FIXTURE_ROOT printed by make-fixture.sh; make-fixture.sh also writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json. Evaluate the target by that exact absolute path — ledger matching is path-exact.
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note
live_ledger_untouched: corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv stays header-only; the builder never writes it (test ledgers live under tests/vault/)

content.identical: cmp -s on the two files exits 0; both sha256sum values equal the constant

declared_ledger_rows.why: full match: both paths exist and both hashes are the actual file bytes

expect.why: byte-identical pair on both sides plus a fully matching ledger row (all four conjuncts)

accept.note: a harness may render the verdict as one token or as verdict+receipt fields; both satisfy this case as long as the verdict class is VERIFIED (never NOT-VERIFIED and never SAFE/NOT-SAFE r2 vocabulary) and the receipt, where printed, is moved-to-obsidian

failure_modes_caught: false NOT-VERIFIED on a fully matching row — the case is the positive control: every conjunct (source path, source sha256, vault path, vault sha256) passes, so any NOT-VERIFIED verdict is a false negative
class collapse: reporting NOT-VERIFIED(none) or NOT-VERIFIED(unreachable) instead of VERIFIED — caught by expect.verdict
r2-vocabulary leakage into the r4 interface (SAFE where the r4 contract says VERIFIED) — caught by must_not_be; the r2 tool itself is covered by crosscheck below

disarmed.method: run with a header-only ledger (e.g. `bash make-fixture.sh --ledger <tmp>/empty.tsv --skip-ledger`, then point the tool's ledger override at that file, or restore tests/vault/ledger-V1.tsv to header-only)
disarmed.why: the row is the receipt: without it the vault copy is not evidence

crosscheck.note: the r2 tool tools/souji-verify.sh predates the r4 VERIFIED vocabulary; for these inputs its expected output is the same verdict pair under r2 names
crosscheck.expected_line: VERDICT	@FIXTURE_ROOT@/source/note.md	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=@FIXTURE_ROOT@/vault/note.md source-sha256=a63192a11325
crosscheck.seam: SOUJI_LEDGER env override (defaults to corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv, which stays header-only)
crosscheck.measured: 2026-10-18: armed run printed exactly the expected_line (SAFE, moved-to-obsidian, exit 0); header-only ledger printed NOT-SAFE none with obsidian=no-matching-ledger-row

determinism.note: fixed content; two builds at different roots produce byte-identical files and equal sha256 values (paths vary per run); the builder asserts the constant and cross-checks this file

build.git: git init -q -b master on <ROOT> (offline, no commits) so the fixture root behaves like a real repo and the pushed receipt must fall through to the ledger
build.safety: never reads or writes the live ledger, the real vault, or any sibling repo; writes only under --out and --ledger FILE

notes: stdout contract: line 1 = JSON {case,root,targets,expect,vault,ledger,sha256}; line 2 = FIXTURE_READY V1 <ROOT> (third token is the ROOT, never the target); --quiet emits KEY=VALUE lines plus the FIXTURE_READY line.
The vault here is a fake vault dir under the fixture root — no Obsidian process, no CLI, no network is involved.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.
